newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends up in narrow-range trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends up in narrow-range trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended a tad firmer on Friday after being trapped in a narrow band for most part of the day, dealers said.
"The market was directionless and did not react to any particular news today," a dealer said.

Another trader said comments by Japan's Economic Planning Agency minister Taro Aso that the economy is gradually recovering failed to inspire trading as this was seen as unlikely to affect Bank of Japan's steady rate policy.
After opening at 21,075, the benchmark SIMEX Nikkei 225 December contract tested crucial technical support at 21,020 on bearish Japanese sentiment over the direction of the economy.
The contract ended at 21,130, up 50 points from its previous close on a turnover of 12,000.
Dealers expected the Nikkei to show some recovery next week towards 21,360 level.
"A break above that could see the contract test 21,400-21,450," a Japanese dealer said.
